claims.claim: The Federal Reserve Board's April 18, 2025 order approving Capital One's acquisition of Discover names the three network subsidiaries being acquired: DFS Services LLC (Discover Network), PULSE Network LLC and Diners Club International Ltd.
claims.quote: These nonbank companies are DFS Services LLC, Riverwoods, Illinois; PULSE Network LLC, Houston, Texas; Diners Club International Ltd., Riverwoods, Illinois
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company, the Merger of Bank Holding Companies, and the Acquisition of Nonbanking Subsidiaries (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footnote 5 of the order. Predates closing (May 18, 2025).

claims.claim: In its application Capital One told the Fed it would move all of its debit-card transactions onto Discover's networks after closing, and a portion of its credit-issuing volume over time.
claims.quote: Capital One, which does not own competing card payment networks, proposes to move all of its debit-card transactions to Discover's card payment networks
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same sentence continues: 'and proposes to move a portion of its credit-card-issuing volume to Discover's networks over time.' Page 15 of the order.

claims.claim: The Fed order records that Discover relies on the Regulation II three-party-system exemption for most debit transactions on its own debit network, which is the regulatory basis for the Capital One debit migration.
claims.quote: Discover relies on this exemption from Regulation II for most debit-card transactions processed by the Discover debit-card payment network.
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footnote 45. Commenters had argued Capital One debit cards could thereby become exempt from the Durbin interchange cap.

claims.claim: The Fed found no significant competitive harm in debit network services because Capital One's post-merger share of debit network purchase volume would be at most 6.9 percent; migrating Capital One debit to Discover would slightly lower debit-network HHI.
claims.quote: The Board's analysis estimates that Capital One's post-merger share of debit-card payment network purchase volume would be no more than 6.9 percent.
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Footnote 46. The order imposes no network-specific structural conditions (no divestiture, routing or pricing conditions on Discover Network, PULSE or Diners Club).

claims.claim: The Fed sized Discover as the fourth-largest credit-card network with 6.4 percent of credit-card payments, and said Capital One credit migration would lower credit-network HHI; DOJ advised it had no adverse comment.
claims.quote: Discover currently operates the fourth largest credit-card payment network, with 6.4 percent of all credit-card payments and approximately 10 percent of credit-card balances and customers.
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page 17. Also: 'The DOJ conducted a review ... and has advised the Board that it has concluded that the proposal does not warrant an adverse comment.'

claims.claim: The Fed approval was conditioned on Capital One's commitment to comply with, and cause subsidiaries to comply with, the separate consent order against Discover and DFS Services LLC over interchange misclassification.
claims.quote: Capital One has committed to comply with the obligations of the Consent Order and to cause any relevant subsidiary to comply
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page 23. Consent order provisions bind DFS and Discover Network 'and their successors and assigns' (consent order para. 13), i.e. Capital One post-close.

claims.claim: The same-day Fed consent order assessed a $100 million civil money penalty on Discover Financial Services and DFS Services LLC (Discover Network) for charging merchants commercial interchange on misclassified consumer cards from 2007 through at least 2023.
claims.quote: The Board of Governors hereby assesses DFS and Discover Network a civil money penalty in the amount of $100,000,000
claims.title: Order to Cease and Desist and Order of Assessment of a Civil Money Penalty Issued Upon Consent (Discover Financial Services; DFS Services LLC), Docket Nos. 25-004-B-HC et al.
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Paragraph 7. Order also requires a written interchange-classification governance plan and quarterly progress reports to the Reserve Bank.

claims.claim: The Fed consent order defines the harmed parties as the acquirers and merchants contracted with Discover Network, and quantifies merchant harm at about one billion dollars, with roughly five million consumer cards classified as commercial at end-2022.
claims.quote: the Firm's Merchant Customers suffered monetary harm of approximately one billion dollars as a result of the Discover Card Interchange Fee Practices
claims.title: Order to Cease and Desist and Order of Assessment of a Civil Money Penalty Issued Upon Consent (Discover Financial Services; DFS Services LLC)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Merchant Customers' is defined as 'merchant acquirers and individual merchants' contracted with Discover Network. At end-2022 about five million consumer cards were classified commercial, ~98% misclassified.

claims.claim: In parallel the FDIC settled with Discover Bank for a $150 million penalty plus merchant restitution the FDIC estimated could exceed $1 billion, which Discover Bank agreed to pay.
claims.quote: a $150 million civil money penalty, and restitution for merchants that paid excess fees. The FDIC estimates the restitution could exceed $1 billion
claims.title: FRB Order No. 2025-10, Order Approving the Acquisition of a Bank Holding Company (Capital One Financial Corporation)
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The OCC's April 18, 2025 approval of the Discover Bank merger into Capital One, N.A. was conditional: within 120 days of consummation Capital One had to file a plan for supervisory non-objection addressing root causes of outstanding Discover Bank enforcement actions and remediation of harm.
claims.quote: Within 120 days of consummation of the Bank Merger, CONA shall provide a plan for supervisory non-objection
claims.title: Conditional Approval Letter for Capital One, National Association to Acquire Discover Bank (OCC Control Number 2024-Combination-336070)
claims.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Section IV 'Condition', enforceable under 12 USC 1818. The OCC letter contains no PULSE- or Diners-specific conditions; the OCC notes the payments network business 'will not reside within CONA'. Press release: https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-36.html

claims.claim: In the OCC record Capital One represented it plans to move all of its debit volume and a meaningful amount of its credit volume onto the Discover networks by 2027.
claims.quote: it plans to move all of its debit card and a meaningful amount of its credit card volumes to the affiliated payments network by 2027
claims.title: Conditional Approval Letter for Capital One, National Association to Acquire Discover Bank
claims.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Appendix p.5. Capital One also cited 'the top three players representing 96 percent of U.S. credit card purchase volume'. This is Capital One's representation as recorded by the regulator, not an enforceable condition.

claims.claim: Capital One's stated network investment commitment, as recorded by the OCC, covers merchant acceptance, brand awareness, technology, network integrity including dispute resolution, and risk/compliance.
claims.quote: COFC will invest significantly in the affiliated payments network's merchant acceptance, brand awareness, technology, network integrity
claims.title: Conditional Approval Letter for Capital One, National Association to Acquire Discover Bank
claims.publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Full phrase continues '(including payment and fraud dispute resolution processes), and risk management and compliance capabilities.' No dollar figure is given in either regulator's document.

claims.claim: Capital One closed the Discover acquisition on May 18, 2025 and said the Discover, PULSE and Diners Club International networks would join its offerings, with Discover-branded credit cards continuing alongside Capital One cards.
claims.quote: The Discover®, PULSE®, and Diners Club International® networks will join our suite of offerings.
claims.title: Capital One Completes Acquisition of Discover
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the 8-K of May 19, 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/927628/000119312525122059/d934475dex991.htm). Release directs to www.capitalonediscover.com.

claims.claim: By its FY2025 10-K (filed February 19, 2026) Capital One reported it had substantially completed reissuing legacy Capital One debit cards onto the Discover-owned Global Payment Network.
claims.quote: The Company has substantially completed the reissuance of legacy Capital One customer debit cards onto the Global Payment Network.
claims.title: Capital One Financial Corporation Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.publisher: Capital One Financial Corporation via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Item 1, Business Developments. Ahead of the 'by 2027' representation made to the OCC.

claims.claim: Capital One now reports a 'Global Payment Network volume' metric, $401.8 billion for 2025, defined as transactions on Discover Network, PULSE, Diners Club and Network Partners.
claims.quote: Global Payment Network volume includes transactions processed on the Discover Network, PULSE Network, Diners Club and Network Partners.
claims.title: Capital One Financial Corporation Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.publisher: Capital One Financial Corporation via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Selected performance metrics table shows 'Global Payment Network volume (3) 401,775' ($ millions) for 2025 with N/A for prior years; likely a partial year from May 18, 2025 close. Network results sit in the Consumer Banking segment.

claims.claim: Capital One's 10-K describes the network fee model for partners: fees paid by acquirers, merchants and issuers, with a pass-through to the bank on its own cards, and defines Network Partners to include fintechs and network-to-network partners.
claims.quote: The Global Payment Network earns fees, which are paid by network participants (primarily acquirers, merchants and issuers)
claims.title: Capital One Financial Corporation Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.publisher: Capital One Financial Corporation via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Glossary: Network Partners are 'Financial institutions, financial technology firms, networks, network-to-network partners and other commercial service providers which we have agreements with for the provision of card issuing, payments processing and related services on the Global Payment Network.' Also: 'For cards issued on the Global Payment Network, a three-party network, the Bank earns an issuer rate instead of interchange fees.'

claims.claim: Capital One flags as a risk that if Regulation II were extended to three-party networks, it would not realize most of the network revenue synergies it expected from the deal; it also lists loss of large merchants on Discover Network or PULSE as a risk.
claims.quote: it could result in the Company not recognizing a significant majority of the network revenue synergies that the Company anticipated
claims.title: Capital One Financial Corporation Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.publisher: Capital One Financial Corporation via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Item 1A. Related risk factor: 'A reduction in the number of large merchants that accept cards on our recently acquired Discover Network or PULSE Network or in the rates they pay could materially adversely affect our business'. Also notes Regulation II routing/exclusivity rules apply 'when third-party issuers issue debit cards on the Global Payment Networks.'

claims.claim: Mastercard's CEO said in January 2025 that Capital One's planned transfer of debit volume to Discover was already built into Mastercard's estimates and was not a surprise.
claims.quote: They have been public about transferring debit volume to the Discover network. There are no surprises fundamentally
claims.title: With The Final OKs, the Capital One-Discover Combo Sets a May 18 Closing
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Quote attributed to Michael Miebach on Mastercard's Q4 2024 call. Article also cites PULSE 2023 volume of $286 billion versus Discover Network $264 billion (Javelin/DT figures). Predates closing.

claims.claim: In September 2025, after closing, a proposed class settlement of merchant lawsuits over Discover's card misclassification was noticed at $540 million to $1.225 billion plus interest, with a merchant claims deadline of May 18, 2026.
claims.quote: Discover has agreed to pay between $540 million and $1.225 billion plus interest in the proposed settlement.
claims.title: A Settlement Is Reached in the Discover Pricing Lawsuits
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: U.S. District Court, N.D. Illinois notice. 'Merchants have until May 18, 2026, to file a payment claim'. Settlement site named: DiscoverMerchantSettlement.com. Postdates Capital One ownership; Discover 'denies the claim'.
